results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response:
The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system, as recorded in VFB. VFB describes the mushroom body as divided into: the calyx, which is closest to the cortex and receives sensory interneuron afferents; the pedunculus, which is a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes; and the mushroom body lobe system, which consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages. 

VFB holds extensive data on the mushroom body, including [2](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of mushroom body") available images, [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body, and [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") parts of the mushroom body. For further information, the user can explore these data, such as listing all available images of the mushroom body, or examining neurons with synaptic terminals in the mushroom body.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila brain contains several types of Kenyon cells. According to VFB, subclasses of [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") include [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses, such as [[KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain")(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open KCab-c(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), KCab-c, [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Kenyon cell of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open Kenyon cell of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"). Additionally, VFB records show that Kenyon cells can be classified into alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which are further subdivided into subtypes. VFB holds 37 records of subclasses of Kenyon cell, as well as other relevant data, including images, scRNAseq data, transgene expression, and connectivity classes.

results.title: Basic connectivity
results.question: What are the main input neurons to the mushroom body?
results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are projection neurons from the antennal lobe and sensory interneuron afferents to the calyx, as stated in the VFB mushroom body description. VFB holds data on neurons with some part in mushroom body, including neurons with synaptic terminals, presynaptic terminals, and postsynaptic terminals in mushroom body, with [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body"), [366](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body"), and [304](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPostsynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with postsynaptic terminals in mushroom body") records respectively. The available data also includes parts of mushroom body and tracts/nerves innervating mushroom body, with [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") and [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,TractsNervesInnervatingHere "Run in VFB: Tracts/nerves innervating mushroom body") records. Additionally, VFB has annotated images of neurons with some part in mushroom body, with [27619](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in mushroom body") records.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior and has a unique anatomy and connectivity, as recorded in VFB. Its large cell body is located posterior to the lower protocerebrum (Koto et al., 1981), and it can be identified by its large descending axon (Power, 1948), which is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective (Koto et al., 1981). The giant fiber neuron enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle (Ito et al., 2014) and descends on the ipsilateral side (Koto et al., 1981; Namiki et al., 2018), in the dorsal cervical fasciculus (Power, 1948). In the brain, it has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center (Kamikouchi et al., 2009; Matsuo et al., 2016), where it receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons (Kim et al., 2020). The giant fiber neuron also arborizes in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget (Matsuo et al., 2016; Namiki et al., 2018). 

The giant fiber neuron enters the ventral nerve cord (VNC) near the dorsal midline and extends posteroventrally to the mesothoracic neuromere, where it turns ventrolaterally, and ends abruptly without branching (Koto et al., 1981). In the mesothoracic neuromere, it forms electrical synapses with downstream motor and premotor neurons at the inframedial bridge, where the two giant fiber neurons connect across the midline, and at the axonal lateral bend (King and Wyman, 1980; Allen et al., 1998; Kennedy and Broadie, 2018). 

VFB records show that the giant fiber neuron is a primary neuron (Allen et al., 1998; Dorkenwald et al., 2024; Schlegel et al., 2024). Available driver lines for the giant fiber neuron include: P{R48A11-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R30C01-p65.AD}, P{R68A06-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD}, P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R14A01-p65.AD}, P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD}, P{VT004455-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R10A12-p65.AD}. Relevant publications for the giant fiber neuron are listed, including Phelan et al., 1996, King and Wyman, 1980, Stürner et al., 2025, Dorkenwald et al., 2024, Namiki et al., 2018, Thomas and Wyman, 1984, Koto et al., 1981, Power, 1948, Ito et al., 2014, Kamikouchi et al., 2009, Kennedy and Broadie, 2018, Allen et al., 1998, Bacon and Strausfeld, 1986, Matsuo et al., 2016, Kim et al., 2020.

VFB holds various data related to the giant fiber neuron, including [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of DNp01, [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNp01") splits targeting DNp01, [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in DNp01, [389](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") downstream connectivity classes for DNp01, and [472](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") upstream connectivity classes for DNp01.
